reason: Run 1 inside the disposable, network-disconnected VM albera-clone-05-lab23b (Windows Server 2025 from the golden image, guest clock set to host time first), driven over PowerShell Direct after owner approval to run #23 only inside a disposable VM. The Broker runs as a real service (albera-windows-broker.exe service <config>), not the lab shim. Guest rollback: 3 services deleted, lab root removed, no unexpected delta. The VM was deleted afterwards. Machine-specific S-1-5-21 SIDs are redacted.
findings: The Control Plane service account cannot OpenProcess the Broker service process with any access (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION included), so the optional server image-hash check is unavailable in service mode (helper returns server_identity_unavailable, pre-send). In production the identity check rests on pipe owner SID + SCM-reported PID; do not configure imageSha256 for service mode.

Both service tokens run at high integrity with TokenElevation=true (normal for service accounts), restricted by their service SID and WRITE RESTRICTED; both tokens also hold SeImpersonatePrivilege and SeCreateGlobalPrivilege. CORRECTED 2026-10-30 (CISO accept condition C1): this finding used to say the Broker needs SeImpersonatePrivilege for the peer check; that was wrong. Those privileges are only the SCM default for a virtual-account service. The peer check opens the client token at SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION (the pipe client sets SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION), which needs no SeImpersonatePrivilege, and the Broker only reads the token user SID. The evidence lines below are the original measurement and are kept as recorded. Each service is to be restricted with `sc privs <svc> SeChangeNotifyPrivilege`; the next lab run asserts that.
